Series::LinearAlgAccessor::cholesky_solve¶

Back to Series::LinearAlgAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series Series::LinearAlgAccessor::cholesky_solve(const Series& b, bool upper = false) const
Series SeriesLinearAlgProxy::cholesky_solve(bool upper = false) const

What It Does¶

Solves A X = B from an already computed Cholesky factor owned by the accessor. If the owner is lower L, the represented matrix is A=L L^T; if it is upper U, A=U^T U. Do not pass the original unfactored matrix.

Reusing A Factorization¶

The solve performs two triangular substitutions. Computing Cholesky once and reusing its factor for many right-hand sides avoids repeating the expensive factorization and preserves the positive-definite structure of the problem.

Parameters And Shapes¶

b is [...,n] or [...,n,k]; a vector result is [...,n,1] and a matrix result preserves [...,n,k]. Batch dimensions broadcast with the factor.

upper selects whether the owner is upper. Its value must match the toggle used to create the factor.

Gradient¶

Reverse mode differentiates both triangular stages. Sensitivities can flow to the factor and to b; the factor sensitivity is restricted to its represented triangle.

Examples¶

Example 1. Factor once, then solve.

auto a = pluss::make_series({{4.0, 2.0}, {2.0, 3.0}});
auto l = a.linearalg.cholesky();
std::cout << l.linearalg.cholesky_solve(pluss::make_series({2.0, 1.0})) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,1], strides=[1,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[[0.5],
  [0]]

Example 2. An upper factor gives the same solution when upper=true.

auto a = pluss::make_series({{4.0, 2.0}, {2.0, 3.0}});
auto u = a.linearalg.cholesky(true);
std::cout << u.linearalg.cholesky_solve(pluss::make_series({2.0, 1.0}), true) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,1], strides=[1,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[[0.5],
  [0]]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The owner is a Cholesky factor, not A itself.

  • A mismatched upper toggle silently describes a different matrix.

  • Zero diagonal entries make the represented system singular.

  • Prefer this method over forming an inverse when only solutions are needed.

See Also¶

  • cholesky: compute the required factor.

  • cholesky_inverse: materialize the represented inverse.
